alerts.reason: A shows reported Q2 net sales grew despite Foodservice weakness. B and C tie part of the 14% Grocery & Snacks volume gain to customers replenishing inventory. If restocking fades as Conagra laps elevated at-home demand, consolidated net sales could fall at least 5% year over year by fiscal Q4.

B shows annual orders fell 27% to $279.6 million, well below the $316.0 million of sales in A. Fewer orders available to ship put Q1 and Q2 sales at risk of a 5% year-over-year decline. A gives only annual sales, so the starting quarterly rate is uncertain.

B says customers requested engagement deferrals and employees had difficulty delivering products and services. Those delays could shift enough revenue out of Q1 or Q2 to produce a new 5% year-over-year decline, though the filing gives neither the amount deferred nor the latest quarterly growth rate.

D says slower activity and the pricing change hurt both revenue and deferred revenue. A shows nine-month revenue still grew 13%. As existing subscriptions run off, weaker deferred revenue could pull a coming quarter's reported revenue at least 5% below the prior year.
